items.title: Palace orders prompt processing of MAIFIP claims
items.description: Malacañang has ordered the Department of Health to work closely with its regional directors and hospitals to ensure the timely processing of legitimate claims under a program designed to assist patients facing financial difficulties.

items.title: Romualdez camp: Ex-speaker not a corruption mastermind
items.description: The camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez insisted that he is not the so-called mastermind of the flood control corruption scheme, saying he only did his part to get the budget approved and has no control over individual projects.

items.title: Sec. Remulla delays trip to France
items.description: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla is delaying his trip to France to block the asylum bid of former lawmaker Zaldy Co.

items.title: How modern tech aids Philippines disaster preparedness
items.description: Modern technology is increasingly aiding disaster preparedness in the Philippines, with the Department of Science and Technology advancing artificial intelligence and other technologies to help save lives even before disasters strike.

items.title: More time needed to resolve impeach vote threshold
items.description: The impeachment court trying Vice President Sara Duterte may defer resolving the voting threshold question to give senators more time to study the issue, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said yesterday.

items.title: ‘No justification for China’s ship ramming’
items.description: The ramming by a China Coast Guard ship of a Philippine civilian vessel can never be justified, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs.

items.title: Next witness to testify on Sara business interests, government deals
items.description: The House prosecution panel is preparing witnesses to testify on Vice President Sara Duterte’s declared business interests, possible government contracts and registered firearms for this week’s impeachment hearings.

items.title: Prompt action sought on repetitive school violence
items.description: Senators are calling for immediate action following another school shooting incident, this time at a high school in South Cotabato that left three students dead on Friday.

items.title: LPG prices also going up
items.description: Consumers can expect higher prices for liquefied petroleum gas and fuel next week, due to ongoing Mideast tensions and the rise in prices of petroleum products in the international market.

items.title: DILG: School shooter was into deep dark web
items.description: The 16-year-old Grade 9 student who went on a shooting rampage at the Banga National High School in South Cotabato on Friday was suffering from depression and was exposed to the deep dark web, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla disclosed yesterday.

items.title: Asian Games open in Nagoya with glitzy ceremony after troubled buildup
items.description: Organizers hope the Asian Games opening ceremony will help resolve a rocky buildup filled with complaints from athletes and officials involving accommodation and transport

items.title: Greenland, Denmark say US deal will not cede sovereignty
items.description: Denmark and Greenland assure sovereignty in US military deal, aiming to enhance Arctic security while respecting self-determination amidst Trump's controversial claims.

items.title: James Reid is finally home, and he’s right where he wants to be
items.description: James had spent much of his career feeling undeserving of all the recognition he was getting. But all along, there was really no need to strive to be anything more — and he would make that groundbreaking realization by fully diving into the music.

items.title: DoE terminates coal block auction
items.description: THE DEPARTMENT of Energy (DoE) will no longer pursue its planned coal block auction this year, which would have included the country’s largest mine operated by Semirara Mining and Power Corp. (SMPC).

items.title: Philippine growth seen picking up in second half — World Bank
items.description: PHILIPPINE ECONOMIC growth could pick up in the second half as public infrastructure spending accelerates and inflation eases, bringing the government’s full-year growth target within closer reach, a World Bank economist said.

items.title: OFW remittances in peril amid Middle East war risks
items.description: REMITTANCE FLOWS from overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) are likely to remain subdued until yearend as overseas deployment slows and renewed hostilities in the Middle East create more volatility, banks said.

items.title: IV of Spades takes top Awit Award nods
items.description: THE four-piece band IV of Spades took home the top prizes — Song of the Year for “Aura” and Album of the Year for Andalucia — at this year’s Awit Awards which were held on Sept. 15 at the SM Mall of Asia Arena in Pasay City. Another track, “Monster,” won Best Sound Engineer Recording.

items.title: Banks’ assets grow at end-July
items.description: ASSETS held by the Philippine banking industry expanded by over 10% year on year as of end-July, driven by sustained growth in lending and deposits, preliminary data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) showed.

items.description: THE Design Center of the Philippines is marking a decade of the International Design Conference (IDC) with its 10th edition on Sept. 18 at the Foro de Intramuros, City of Manila, bringing together leading voices from the Philippines and around the world to look at how design can respond to the complexity and diversity of the world we live in.
